results.reason: Identifies five-year automatic renewal under §2.2 and the 270/240-day window (Oct. 3 – Nov. 2, 2026) against June 30, 2027. It explains the lock-in with the higher minimum and no termination for convenience. It recommends negotiating an amendment or sending a protective non-renewal notice before the deadline.

States the §5.3 30-day objection window running from Aug. 21 receipt to about Sept. 20, notes the increase is 'deemed accepted', and says the right has almost certainly lapsed. It advises confirming with the client whether an objection was sent and using leverage to negotiate.

Explains that the §11.1 indemnity reaches product-defect claims and is uncapped (citing the amended §12.3(a)), while Brightmere's §11.2 is narrow and capped. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own fault and adding §11.2 to the cap carve-outs.

Identifies that Amend. §3.1 deletes the former §12.3(b) recall carve-out, so recall reimbursement is now under the 12-month cap, which a large recall could exceed. It recommends reinstating the carve-out.

Identifies Amend. §6 Delaware law and Wilmington forum, the conflict with Agmt §§17.1–17.2 (New York County), and that the Amendment prevails under §1.4. It recommends restoring New York law and forum.
States the Notice was delivered Aug. 21, 2026.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States the Amendment outranks the Agreement body under Agmt §1.4.
Formatted as a memorandum to the Supervising Partner, with Where / Why it matters / Fix for each issue.
Concludes the recall reimbursement is now capped.
Expressly acknowledges that the Delaware provisions now govern.
